messages.content: We’re starting to look at the central Oregon coast for six nights in early September. It will be the two of us, and we can move the dates by up to two days. The whole trip needs to stay around $4,400.
With flights into Portland and a rental car, how much of that would you like to reserve for lodging? Also, should I compare oceanfront places against less expensive stays a short distance inland?
Use about $2,700 as the lodging ceiling. Please compare both. We still need room for flights, the car, and meals, so I don’t want a place that only looks affordable before fees.

I’ll compare six-night windows of September 2-8, September 4-10, and September 6-12, 2027. I’ll include mandatory property charges, taxes, deposits, cancellation terms, and when payment is due. Are Newport and Yachats both acceptable bases?
Yes. We’ll have the car, and either one works. Beach access matters more than being in the middle of town.

I found three useful contrasts: Shoreline Headlands Hotel in Newport is oceanfront with direct beach access; Alder Street Inn in Yachats is two blocks inland with a marked route to the beach; and Pacific Window Cottage south of Yachats is a highly rated rental with a full kitchen. I’m checking the three date windows on a complete-price basis.
Good. The cottage sounds appealing, but be careful about the payment schedule. We’re still several months out.

The September 6-12 window is cheapest at all three. Complete lodging totals are $1,949.30 at Shoreline Headlands, $1,136.69 at Alder Street, and $1,834.90 at Pacific Window Cottage. Those totals include every mandatory charge shown at checkout.
What happens on the other dates? I don’t want to shift just because the nightly rate is lower if there’s some fee hiding in it.

For September 2-8, the totals are $2,044.39 at Shoreline Headlands, $1,170.32 at Alder Street, and $1,931.33 at the cottage. For September 4-10, they rise to $2,227.78, $1,264.49, and $2,079.85 respectively. There are no additional required charges beyond those totals, although optional pet, housekeeping, and damage-protection products are excluded.
Break down the September 6 option, especially the oceanfront hotel and the rental.

Shoreline Headlands is $248 per night, or $1,488 for six nights. Its mandatory resort fee is $39 per night, adding $234. Tax is $227.30, producing a $1,949.30 total. Parking and beach access are included. The resort fee cannot be removed even if you do not use its fitness room or welcome-drink benefit.
And the cottage?

Pacific Window Cottage has $1,320 in rent, a $175 cleaning charge, a $159 host service charge, and $180.90 in lodging tax, for $1,834.90. It has a full kitchen and one parking space. The listing describes beach access as a seven-minute walk along a residential lane, but it is not oceanfront.
That location is fine. For beach trips with my partner, walking distance to the beach is the cutoff I want you to use. It doesn’t have to be directly oceanfront unless I specifically ask for that.

Understood. Both the cottage and Alder Street meet that threshold; Shoreline Headlands adds direct access rather than merely qualifying on location. The payment terms create the more important difference here.
Lay those out for all three. Also tell me whether the cheaper inn has any mandatory parking or destination charge.

Shoreline Headlands charges one night plus tax, $325.74, at booking. The balance is collected at check-in, and cancellation is penalty-free until 4 p.m. local time seven days before arrival. Alder Street charges the first night with tax, $189.45, at booking; the remainder is due at arrival, with free cancellation until 6 p.m. local time three days before arrival. It has free parking and no resort, destination, or cleaning fee.
And the rental’s full-payment issue?

The cottage requires the entire $1,834.90 at booking. Cancellation returns 100% through June 15, 50% from June 16 through July 31, and nothing from August 1 onward. The platform’s optional damage coverage is not included in the total, but declining it requires a refundable $500 card hold shortly before arrival.
That’s more restrictive than I want this early. Use a rough trip estimate of $850 for both flights, $520 for the car, and $650 for meals. Which two lodging choices leave a sensible margin?

Using the cheapest September 6-12 window, Shoreline Headlands produces an estimated trip total of $3,969.30, leaving $430.70 under the $4,400 cap. Alder Street produces a $3,156.69 total, leaving $1,243.31. The cottage would total $3,854.90 and leave $545.10, but its full prepayment and steep cancellation schedule make it a weaker choice despite the kitchen.

So keep the oceanfront hotel as the location-first option and the inn as the budget option. I’m not ready to choose dates or book anything. Give me the final comparison and the exact items we need to recheck later.

Keep Shoreline Headlands and Alder Street Inn for September 6-12, with nothing booked. Shoreline Headlands is $1,949.30 complete and leaves $430.70 in the trip budget; its direct beach access costs $812.61 more than Alder Street. Alder Street is $1,136.69 complete, has no mandatory property fee, includes parking, and is two blocks from the beach, leaving $1,243.31 for price changes or additional spending. Drop Pacific Window Cottage for now because it requires full payment and becomes nonrefundable August 1. Before booking, reprice both hotels for all three date windows, confirm taxes and mandatory fees at checkout, verify the beach route from Alder Street remains open, confirm parking is still included, and recheck each deposit and cancellation deadline. The September 6 dates currently offer the best totals, but no dates or lodging have been selected.
